issues.text: 23 in 100 lost it before arriving and never regained it.
issues.problem: 'Never' overstates: the study measured only to discharge.
issues.source_says: 23% declined between baseline and admission and failed to recover to baseline function between admission and discharge.
issues.replacement: 23 in 100 lost it before arriving and had not regained it by discharge.

issues.text: The data are old, but a 2019 review found about 3 in 10 still lose independence.
issues.problem: Omits outcome and setting of the review (basic daily activities after an acute hospital stay).
issues.source_says: Loyd 2019: pooled prevalence of hospital-associated disability 30% in adults 65+ in acute care.
issues.replacement: The data are over 20 years old, but a 2019 review found about 3 in 10 older people still lose independence in daily activities after an acute hospital stay.

issues.text: In a US study of 2,293 older medical inpatients, 35 in 100 went home less able to wash, dress or use the toilet than two weeks before admission. Most had lost it before arrival.
issues.problem: Omits the qualifications (age 70+, reported by patient or relative, data over 20 years old) that every other version carries.
issues.source_says: C05-01-a/e qualifications: self or surrogate report; published 2003.
issues.replacement: In a US study of 2,293 medical inpatients aged 70+ (data over 20 years old), 35 in 100 went home less able to wash, dress or use the toilet than two weeks before admission. Most had lost it before arrival.

issues.text: In older women in Baltimore, changing method without difficulty went with slower walking and later difficulty. A Finnish study agreed.
issues.problem: Population limits (more able women aged 70 to 80, recruited in the 1990s) must appear in every version (C05-02-e).
issues.source_says: 436 women 70-80 among the two-thirds least disabled; enrolled 1994-95.
issues.replacement: In more able women aged 70 to 80 in Baltimore (1990s), changing method without difficulty went with slower walking and later difficulty. A smaller Finnish study agreed.

issues.text: In a Baltimore study of women aged 70 to 80 (1990s),
issues.problem: Omits that these were the more able two thirds of their age group.
issues.source_says: 'among the two-thirds least disabled living in the community'.
issues.replacement: In a Baltimore study of more able women aged 70 to 80 (1990s),

issues.text: Improvement was real, though, and it was most common early.
issues.problem: False as written: more frail people improved (about 43 in 100 moved to a less frail stage) than prefrail people (23 in 100). What was more common from the early stage was reaching no frailty signs at all.
issues.source_says: Prefrail to robust 23.1%; frail to robust 3.3%, frail to prefrail 40.3%.
issues.replacement: Improvement was real, though, and getting back to no signs of frailty was far more common from the early stage.

issues.text: In 16 studies of 42,775 older people living at home, followed for about 4 years, 14 in 100 became less frail, 29 in 100 became more frail, and 57 in 100 stayed the same.
issues.problem: Missing required qualification that figures use one definition of frailty (phenotype); present on visual and LinkedIn only.
issues.source_says: C05-07-a qualifications: one definition, people living at home.
issues.replacement: In 16 studies of 42,775 older people living at home, followed for about 4 years, 14 in 100 became less frail, 29 in 100 became more frail, and 57 in 100 stayed the same (one definition of frailty).

issues.text: "CFS 6 (heart failure; needs standby help to wash)"
issues.problem: Invented illustrative example not labelled as such in the caption.
issues.source_says: C05-16-d: two-person comparison must be labelled illustrative.
issues.replacement: "CFS 6 (heart failure; needs standby help to wash)", to take an invented example,

issues.text: 9: expected to live under about 6 months
issues.problem: Omits that level 9 applies only to people not otherwise severely frail; readers may equate 9 with 'worse than 8'.
issues.source_says: Level 9: life expectancy <6 months, who are not otherwise living with severe frailty.
issues.replacement: 9: expected to live under about 6 months, not otherwise severely frail

issues.text: A US trial sent an occupational therapist, a nurse and a handyperson to 300 older people on low incomes,
issues.problem: Only 152 of the 300 randomised got the programme; the rest had social visits.
issues.source_says: 300 randomised: CAPABLE n=152, attention control n=148.
issues.replacement: A US trial of 300 older people on low incomes sent an occupational therapist, a nurse and a handyperson to about half of them,

issues.text: A US trial sent an occupational therapist, a nurse and a handyperson to 300 older people on low incomes.
issues.problem: As X: only half received the programme.
issues.source_says: CAPABLE n=152, control n=148.
issues.replacement: A US trial of 300 older people on low incomes sent an occupational therapist, a nurse and a handyperson to about half of them.

issues.text: A US trial sent an occupational therapist, nurse and handyperson to 300 older people on low incomes. At 5 months they had less difficulty washing and dressing, but it faded by 12 months.
issues.problem: Only half received it; comparator missing.
issues.source_says: CAPABLE n=152 vs social-visit control n=148.
issues.replacement: A US trial of 300 older people on low incomes sent an occupational therapist, nurse and handyperson to half. At 5 months they had less difficulty washing and dressing than those given social visits, but it faded by 12 months.

issues.text: 8 in 10 said it made life easier, against 4 in 10.
issues.problem: Omits 'a great deal' and that this is a survey of those who answered.
issues.replacement: 8 in 10 who answered said it made life easier a great deal, against 4 in 10.

issues.text: In 29 hospital trials of 13,766 people, about 60 in 100 were alive and at home 3 to 12 months later with CGA, against 56 in 100 without.
issues.problem: The per-100 figures come from subsets of trials (16 trials, 6,799 people for living at home; 14 for care home; 21 for deaths), not all 29 trials/13,766 people.
issues.source_says: RR 1.06 (16 trials, 6799); nursing home RR 0.80 (14 trials, 6285); mortality RR 1.00 (21 trials, 10,023).
issues.replacement: In a Cochrane review of 29 hospital trials, about 60 in 100 were alive and at home 3 to 12 months later with CGA, against 56 in 100 without (16 trials reported this).

issues.text: 29 trials, 13,766 older people, 3 to 12 months
issues.problem: Kicker implies every bar pools all 29 trials; each outcome comes from 14 to 21 trials.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Cochrane review of 29 trials; each result from 14 to 21 trials; 3 to 12 months

issues.text: Bar chart from a Cochrane review of 29 hospital trials, 13,766 older people, at 3 to 12 months, per 100 people:
issues.problem: Same denominator issue.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Bar chart from a Cochrane review of 29 hospital trials (each result from 14 to 21 trials), at 3 to 12 months, per 100 people:

issues.text: For frail people at home, 21 studies showed little or no difference in deaths or care home moves.
issues.problem: Drops the possible reduction in unplanned admissions and certainty wording; reads as evidence of no benefit (C05-08-g).
issues.source_says: Mortality 'probably' little or no difference (moderate); may decrease unplanned admissions (low certainty).
issues.replacement: For frail people at home, 21 studies showed probably little or no difference in deaths or care home moves, and possibly fewer unplanned admissions (weak evidence).

issues.text: For frail people living at home, 21 studies showed little or no difference in deaths or care home moves;
issues.problem: Mortality finding is moderate certainty ('probably').
issues.source_says: CGA probably leads to little or no difference in mortality (moderate certainty).
issues.replacement: For frail people living at home, 21 studies showed probably little or no difference in deaths or care home moves;

issues.text: for almost 9 in 10 pairs, agreement was only weak to moderate (kappa 0.10 to 0.83 overall).
issues.problem: About 8 in 100 pairs had kappa below 0.2 (worse than weak); 'at most moderate' is accurate.
issues.source_says: Almost 90% of 595 pairs had kappa under 0.6; 7.6% under 0.2.
issues.replacement: for almost 9 in 10 pairs, agreement was moderate at best (kappa 0.10 to 0.83 overall).

issues.text: For almost 9 in 10 pairs of tools, agreement on who was frail was only weak to moderate.
issues.problem: As X.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: For almost 9 in 10 pairs of tools, agreement on who was frail was moderate at best.

issues.text: Pooled estimates put physical definitions at about 1 in 8 and tools counting many health problems at about 1 in 4.
issues.problem: O'Caoimh pooled studies including people aged 50+; qualification missing.
issues.source_says: O'Caoimh 2021: population studies, ages 50+; 12% physical, 24% frailty index.
issues.replacement: Pooled estimates from studies of people aged 50 and over put physical definitions at about 1 in 8 and tools counting many health problems at about 1 in 4.
